findings.message: The round-2 fix made the confirm path's non-`run` decided steps best-effort so that a trace-store failure can't hide an outcome that is already settled. The cancel path was missed. `cancelAction` awaits `decidedStep(action, "cancelled")` after `cancelCard` has already claimed the key as cancelled. If that trace insert fails, the exception goes to `cancelChat`/`outcomeOf`, and the person sees an error for a cancel that did take effect. Fix: make the cancel's decided step best-effort and log its failure, the same as `decide()` does for confirm. Add a variant row for cancel to decided-trace-fail.test.ts.
findings.scenario: The trace store is down while the person presses Cancel → the key is claimed `cancelled`, but cancelChat returns an error state. A retry then gets NotPendingError(decision: cancelled). The UI never said 'Cancelled' even though it was.

findings.message: In the write-tool shim in `runTurn`, the card goes into `pending` before `await traceStep({ kind: "pending" ... })` runs. If that step write throws, the tool call fails toward the model, but the card was already pushed and `append` still saves it. The person is shown a live confirm card while the model replies that the action failed. This is the same 'a trace failure must not change the outcome' class that the registry and confirm paths fixed. Fix: write the step before the push, so the card is dropped when the step fails. Or keep the push and make the step best-effort, but don't do both halves.
findings.scenario: The trace insert fails while the model calls rotate_secret → the model is told the tool errored and says 'I couldn't do that', yet the chat shows a 'Rotate GitHub' confirm card that can be confirmed.

findings.message: Every row that isn't revoked, including expired ones, gets the prompt 'Rotate the X token, keep its expiry'. For an expired credential, `keptExpiry` always throws, and only on confirm, after the person has typed the new secret into the masked field. So the main action on the rows that most need attention can never succeed as offered. Fix: for expired rows, use a prompt that asks for a new expiry date, or check `keptExpiry` when the card is proposed (before the confirm) so the card asks for `expiresAt` up front.
findings.scenario: The Azure DevOps credential shows Expired (expiresAt 2026-10-01) → Ask to rotate → the model proposes rotate_secret with no expiresAt → the person types the new token and confirms → ToolError 'expiry has passed'. The value is discarded and nothing is rotated.

findings.message: Rounds 2–3 fixed the Scheduler tickets so each pin resolves to exactly the rows its ticket counts (`withInLatest`, a status filter). The Keys tickets were left behind: 'Expiring in 30 days', 'Rotated in 90 days' and 'Credentials' all pin `list_secrets` with `{}`, which returns every credential. Fix: give `list_secrets` a filter (for example `expiringWithinDays` or status) and pin each ticket with the filter it counts.
findings.scenario: With 6 credentials and 1 expiring, pinning 'Expiring in 30 days' (value 1) hands chat all 6 credentials. 'Rotate the ones in this pin' then targets 6 records instead of 1.

findings.message: The 'expiring soon' rule is written a second time. The hub computes `r.status === "active" && expiresAt - Date.now() <= EXPIRY_WINDOW_DAYS*DAY`, while KeyTickets and KeyTable use `expiringSoon(r, now)` from keys/format.ts. The hub version also accepts an active credential whose expiry has already passed but hasn't been swept yet, and reports a day count of zero or less. Fix: use the one `expiringSoon` helper in both places.
findings.scenario: An active credential with expiresAt one hour ago (sweep not run yet) → the hub lede says 'the X credential expires in 0 days' with a '1 expiring' chip, while the Keys screen classifies the same row differently.

findings.message: The dock's 'New conversation' button has its own copy of the new-chat logic. Unlike the new `newChat()`, it doesn't close History or reset `fields`. Call `newChat()` from both places.
findings.scenario: Open History, then press the dock's New conversation button → the log clears but the History panel stays open and the conversation log stays hidden.

findings.message: Each part's `order by seq` sits inside a subquery, and the outer `select * from (...) r where r.tenant_id = ...` has no ORDER BY. Postgres doesn't guarantee the row order of the exported NDJSON. Put the order by on the outer query.
`null` stands for both 'no database' and 'the usage query failed', and either way the chat footer is hidden. A failed lookup should show as unknown, not vanish.
findings.scenario: ai.call query times out → the footer disappears with no sign that usage couldn't be loaded.

findings.message: Every pin on the page (each data-class row, the provider and subprocessor cards, all four tickets) resolves to `get_ai_policy` with `{}`, so each one returns the whole policy rather than the row or metric it sits on. Pass a key, for example `{ class: r.cls }`, so the pin points at its own record.
When `groupBy` is absent, `key` is silently ignored and the full result comes back. Reject a `key` that has no `groupBy`.
findings.scenario: get_ai_usage {key:'2026-10-03'} → a whole month's data instead of one day.

findings.message: An empty `set_ai_policy` patch still bumps the policy version, writes an audit row and emits ai.policy.updated, even though nothing changed. Refuse an empty patch.
findings.scenario: set_ai_policy {} → Policy v7 becomes v8 with no change.

findings.message: The added 047, 049 and 048 mock sections never close their `<section>` (047 also leaves its confirm-card `<div>` open), so the 048, 049 and 050 sections nest inside 047. Separately, the module standard says the mock is read-only during a build, and this change edits it.

The hub's AI usage card builds its cost from aiStats and shows `$${s.costUsd.toFixed(2)} this month`. That folds unpriced calls in as $0. The AI usage screen and get_ai_usage use aiUsage/costLabel, which report those calls as unknown and never as $0 (048 AC-5). That makes two copies of the month's cost total, and they disagree. Fix: build the hub card from aiUsageTotals(scope tenant) and costLabel.
findings.scenario: Every call this month used a model with no price → the hub card reads "$0.00 this month" while /settings/ai/usage reads "Unknown".

findings.message: The 052 fix made findSchedule refuse an ambiguous title rather than write to the first match. entityId has the same flaw and was not fixed: it resolves a legal entity by case-insensitive name and takes the first row in name order. set_entity_zone then writes the zone to that entity and moves all of its schedules. Fix: when more than one entity matches the name, refuse and list the candidates (by id), as findSchedule does.
findings.scenario: A tenant with two entities named "Lumen Labs" (AU and LK), and the person asks to set Lumen Labs' zone to Australia/Sydney → whichever row sorts first gets the zone, possibly the LK entity, and its schedules are re-zoned without anyone naming it.

findings.message: settings_overview with an unknown `area` returns [], so a pin that no longer matches looks like an empty but valid answer. The other read tools in this diff throw notFound in that case. Fix: throw notFound when `area` is given and nothing matches.

USAGE_SOURCES covers only chat, agent and job. Under "All sources", calls with any other source (for example ui or mcp, if the gateway logs them) count toward the Cost ticket, but the per-source breakdown note leaves them out, and no filter can select them.
findings.scenario: An MCP-sourced AI call costing $2 → the Cost ticket shows $2 more than the sum in its own note.
